Subject: ClarifyTech - Redwood partner tech validation: initial architecture and POC ask

Hi Ben — great to meet on the call earlier. Quick recap and asks from our side:

- Attached is our integration draft (claritytech-redwood-arch-v1.pdf) that shows how we plan to call Redwood for transcript-enhanced summarization and reranking.
- Primary goals: low-latency snippet generation (<=250ms 95th for short queries), safe model output, and a plan for customers that require on-prem/private deployment.
- We want Redwood to validate 3 main areas: authentication pattern for our multi-tenant connector, streaming behavior for client-side partial renders, and guidance on model+quantization profile for cost/latency.
- Proposed POC: 2-week technical validation with a small traffic replay (see sample-calls.jsonl attached). We can provide a dataset and a test harness.

Questions:
1) Is Redwood comfortable validating private deploy constraints (KMS, network isolation) as part of the POC?
2) Who on your side should we include for the architecture deep-dive?

Attaching: claritytech-redwood-arch-v1.pdf, sample-calls.jsonl, infra-diagrams.png

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

— Clara Ng

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-14T14:50:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: ClarifyTech tech validation - quick review notes

Internal notes (do not forward verbatim to partner) — reading Clara's samples and infra diagram:

On Tue, Jan 12, Clara Ng wrote:
> Sample traffic profile (sample-calls.jsonl): 200 rps simulated with spikes to 600 rps during peak. Typical token length: 30-120 tokens per call.
> Compliance: many of our customers require SOC2 and customer-managed keys; we'll need a clear path for evidence during the POC.

Checklist / concerns:
- Auth: Multi-tenant connector should use per-tenant API keys + RBAC mapping. Validate that token rotation fits into our connector TTLs.
- Streaming: Their UX expects partial tokens delivered within 250ms p95 for short queries. We'll need to run a streaming micro-benchmark using their harness; continuous batching could impact p95 unless we pin small-batch fast-paths.
- KV cache compatibility: If they plan to do long conversation contexts, confirm that our KV cache semantics (eviction, shard-locality) don't cause tail-latency spikes under their spike workload.
- Quantization: Recommend trying int8 Q4_0 first for latency; we should prepare a quality regression test set.
- Private deployment: Confirm KMS integration patterns (Vault, AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) and whether they require HSM-backed keys. If they want an appliance image, evaluate sysreqs and packaging effort.

Action items for POC runbook:
1) Pre-POC baseline: run 1-hour replay at 200rps, measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming partial events.
2) Stress run: 30-minute spike to 600rps to observe tail behavior.
3) Regression evals: run quality checks across 200 curated prompts (Clara to provide).
4) Security checklist: SOC2 evidence pack and KMS test plan; loop in Security if appliance required.

I'll draft the technical runbook and attach partner-tech-qa.md. Marissa — can you own scheduling and the HubSpot deal updates?

-- Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[karthik signature]

[Attachment: partner-tech-qa.md (text/markdown)]
